flags.headline: PGY -5.88% Friday; part of a multi-week derate on rate/credit-cycle repricing
flags.detail: PGY closed Friday 9/25 at $17.62, -5.88% on the day, continuing a slide from ~$21.11 on 8/11 (about -16.5% over six weeks). GuruFocus attributes the Friday move to the stock 'fully pricing in the current higher-for-longer interest rate environment.' Separately, subprime auto-loan delinquencies hit 6.8% at the start of 2026, a 32-year high, per Pagaya's own Q1 2026 disclosures, though the company states its own personal-loan and auto portfolios remain within historical ranges. No PGY-specific negative print or 8-K found for this week. Note: a Nasdaq-syndicated headline claiming PGY 'collapsed 84.8% in September' is not corroborated by actual price history ($21.11 -> $17.62 is a ~17% move) and is disregarded as an unreliable aggregator artifact rather than used as evidence, per the guardrail against fabricated/unconfirmed data.
flags.thesis_link: Matches key_risk: 'Credit cycle deterioration -- rising consumer delinquencies would disproportionately impair Pagaya's portfolio of borrowers rejected by traditional credit models, potentially reversing six consecutive profitable quarters.' The rate/delinquency backdrop cited above is the macro precursor to that risk, not yet a confirmed deterioration in Pagaya's own book.

flags.headline: HUT -4.56% Friday with no negative catalyst found; UBS upgraded it the same week
flags.detail: HUT closed Friday 9/25 down 4.56-4.7% depending on source, with no company-specific bad news identified. Held at AMBER on the magnitude of the move pending an explanation, consistent with this routine's prior treatment of unexplained single-day declines in this name's volatility band.
